title: Terra VPC Edge Wrangler: subnet/NAT/Endpoint controller & upgrade hooks
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (terra-vpc-edge-wrangler) that standardizes VPC topology for Private deployments and includes: AZ-aware subnet roles, deterministic NAT/IGW allocation, VPC endpoints (interface & gateway) with tight endpoint policies, explicit route table wiring, and built-in upgrade / canary hooks plus health probes. The module should be consumable by Customer/private stacks, support pinning of route behavior (eg. central egress vs per-vpc NAT), work with our existing state backend (S3+Dynamo lock), and provide observability hooks (CloudWatch metrics for endpoint and egress health). This ticket covers module design, impl, CI pipeline for canary upgrades, and a lightweight synthetic health check implementation for endpoint & NAT availability.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs: az_list, subnet_roles (public/ingress/private/egress), nat_mode (single-az|per-az|central), endpoint_map (service->config), route_policies, and tags
Default output includes: vpc_id, subnet_ids_by_role_and_az, nat_gateway_ids, igw_id, endpoint_ids, route_table_ids
Canary upgrade flow: terraform plan/apply can be targeted at single AZ/unexpected-change guard rails and has a documented rollback path
Automated health checks: Lambda (or Fargate) probe publishes CloudWatch metrics for each endpoint and NAT egress path; alarms created for degraded state
CI pipeline runs plan against a disposable workspace and requires manual approval to apply to production/private workspaces
Module has integration tests (local terratest or GH Actions with ephemeral AWS account) that validate routing and endpoint connectivity
Documentation (README + design doc) exists and conforms to infra module standards and includes upgrade checklist
implementation_notes: Core TF resources: aws_vpc, aws_subnet (one per AZ x role), aws_internet_gateway, aws_eip, aws_nat_gateway, aws_route_table, aws_route_table_association, aws_vpc_endpoint (interface and gateway), aws_vpc_endpoint_route_table_association
Subnet role mapping: input map role -> cidr_block_template and az_priority to support graceful AZ rollouts
NAT allocation: support both nat_mode=per-az (recommended) and nat_mode=single-az with automatic EIP allocation + wait_for (create before destroy) to avoid transient blackholes
Endpoint policies: accept json_policy var or reference to centralized policy library for common services (s3,kms,ssm). Enforce least privilege by default
Routing model: create isolated route tables per private-subnet role and attach explicit routes to NAT/IGW/Endpoints; do not implicitly rely on default route propagation

Upgrade hooks: provide null_resource triggers with local-exec that call a controlled 'preflight' lambda (HTTP) and 'postflight' checks. These hooks are NO-OP by default and enabled via a module flag (enable_upgrade_hooks)

Health checks: pack a small Lambda that performs: DNS resolution for endpoint private IPs, TCP connect on service ports, and a curl to a known backend via NAT to validate egress. Lambda publishes a custom metric per resource and a composite CloudWatch alarm is created
State considerations: require S3 backend + DynamoDB lock. Module will emit a required provider_version and recommend running terraform 1.6+; include guidance for migration patches in README
Security: ensure endpoints with interface type get security_group_ids var and default to security group that allows only outbound to our service subnets. Mark security_review_required
Observability: write metrics namespace 'Redwood/VPC/EdgeWrangler' and provide a dashboard snippet for latency and health counts
Testing: add a GH Actions job that runs 'terraform init/plan' and invokes the health-lambda integration test in a sandbox account. Terratest is preferred for deeper validation but optional for MVP
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: creating NAT+EIP across many accounts increases IP usage. Mitigation: add variable to cap eip_pool_size and warn in plan when near account limits

Risk: during upgrades an apply could disrupt routes. Mitigation: enforce canary step (single AZ) and put route replacements behind create_before_destroy and lifecycle ignore_changes for ephemeral tags
Risk: endpoint policy misconfiguration could open data exfiltration paths. Mitigation: default to deny-all and require explicit allow rules; run policy linter in CI
Risk: health probes increase API calls and cost. Mitigation: probes run at low cadence (5m) and are configurable per-deployment
Risk: private endpoints rely on correct DNS. Mitigation: include optional Route53 private zone validation step in preflight
